original_question: For every pair of positive integers k and n, determine whether there exists a dimension d=d(k,n) such that every Ramsey set X of size at most n, regardless of the Euclidean space containing X, appears as a monochromatic congruent copy inside every k-colouring of R^d.
target_in_paper: Section 12, Conjecture 12.1, "A boundedness conjecture for Ramsey sets."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the main quantifier structure of the paper’s conjecture: for each pair of positive integers k and n, one asks for a dimension bound d=d(k,n) that depends only on k and n; the bound is uniform over all Ramsey sets X with at most n points; X may live in an arbitrary Euclidean space; and every k-colouring of R^d should contain a monochromatic congruent copy of X.
missing_details: The paper first defines a Ramsey set: a finite set X in some Euclidean space is Ramsey if for every r in N there exists D in N such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X.
It should be stated explicitly that X is finite and that |X| means its cardinality.
The ambient Euclidean space containing X should be written separately, e.g. X\subseteq R^m for some m, to avoid confusion with the size parameter n and the target dimension d.
The ambient field/space is the real Euclidean space R^m, not an arbitrary metric space or vector space.
A k-colouring means a colouring of all points of R^d with k colours.
It should be explicit that d depends only on k and n, and not on the particular Ramsey set X or on the ambient dimension m in which X is originally embedded.
For a stand-alone formulation, "monochromatic congruent copy" should be understood as a subset of R^d congruent (isometric) to X whose points all receive the same colour.
The paper states this as a conjecture, so a paper-faithful rewrite should ask whether this boundedness statement holds, rather than broaden it into a more general classification problem.
refined_question: Is the following boundedness conjecture for Euclidean Ramsey sets true? For every k,n in N, does there exist d=d(k,n) in N such that, whenever X is a finite Ramsey set with |X|\le n lying in some Euclidean space R^m, every k-colouring of R^d contains a monochromatic subset congruent to X? Here, X is called Ramsey if for every r in N there exists D in N such that every r-colouring of R^D contains a monochromatic congruent copy of X.
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of the exact open problem stated in Section 12 as Conjecture 12.1. The sentence immediately before the conjecture supplies the operative definition of a Ramsey set, and the surrounding context shows that the paper’s intent is a uniform boundedness question for Ramsey sets of bounded cardinality, not the broader neighboring problems about characterizing Ramsey sets as spherical or as subsets of transitive sets. No explicit equivalent reformulation is given nearby, so the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is simply a self-contained restatement of Conjecture 12.1 with the definition of Ramsey set built in.
